tex_content.html:
Proposition
[$(\mathcal{M},\dGH )$ separable and complete]

Source: petersen:page-0412, petersen:page-0413 ↗ rem:pet-ch11-gh-pseudo-metric-quotient 1. ch11:11.1.8The quotient metric space $(\mathcal{M},\dGH )$ is both separable and complete.
Proof

↗ prop:pet-ch11-gh-space-separable-complete \sketch Finite metric spaces are dense by subsection 1.1, and perturbing their distance matrices to rational ones gives a countable dense family. For completeness, take a subsequence with $\dGH (X_i,X_{i+1})<2^{-i}$, choose corresponding admissible metrics, and glue them along the chain. The completion of the resulting union contains compact closures $Y_i$ isometric to $X_i$, with $d_H(Y_i,Y_{i+1})<2^{-i}$. These closures converge in Hausdorff distance to a compact set $Y$, hence $X_i\to Y$ in $\dGH $.
